name: Bright Sky Blue
lede: Bright Sky Blue is a vivid, slightly greenish cyan blue, a descriptive name more than a historical one.

sections.title: A descriptive name
sections.body:
The name is a plain description: bright, plus [[sky-blue]]. Our sources list it in the 2010 xkcd color survey [1]. The swatch is far more saturated than a real sky, and the nearest ISCC-NBS name is "brilliant greenish blue" at a distance of 7.1 [1].

The words do turn up in the books. Finlay saw bright sky blues from [[indigo]] in the early Indian painted and printed cottons at the Victoria and Albert Museum's 2015 exhibition [2]. St Clair's glossary defines [[azure]] as a bright sky blue, used in heraldry [3]. Neither passage describes this exact swatch.

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our 23,781-painting archive has this color covering at least 1 percent of its canvas, as photographed [4]. That describes our archive, not painting as a whole. For a bright blue that does appear, see [[deep-sky-blue]] and [[cerulean]].
